11.2b — Create PT: Submit as Final

Today the Create PT becomes COLLEGE BOARD PROPERTY. You will open the Digital Portfolio, upload the program, the video, and the written responses, and press the button your teacher cannot press for you. Then — a unit's worth of weight off — we pivot to the exam itself.

Submission ~35 min

What goes in the Digital Portfolio (all five, in order):

  1. Program code (the .zip or the single file): your whole project — including the lines your PPR cites, verbatim
  2. Video: your sub-60s one take (11.2a)
  3. WR1: purpose + abstraction
  4. WR2a / WR2b / WR2c: algorithm, development story, list — copy carefully from your 11.1e drafts into the Portfolio's text boxes (they paste PLAIN text — check formatting after pasting)
  5. PPR: uploaded as your exam-day reference

The final final check — read aloud with a partner:

  • WR text in the Portfolio == WR text in your plan (pasting drops things — VERIFY, do not trust)
  • Every code excerpt in the PPR exists verbatim in the submitted program
  • Video plays from the Portfolio preview (not just your disk)
  • No names, no school, no faces without permission forms

Then Submit as Final. The deadline is April 30, 11:59 PM ET — you are submitting EARLY, because upload failures happen and the Portfolio does not care whose fault. Take the confirmation screenshot (yes, really) and put it in your repo: commit "11.2b: SUBMITTED".

Bug Hunt: Portfolio traps

  1. The Portfolio says "draft" even after you think you submitted. Which button did you miss — and why is a screenshot the only proof?
  2. Your WR2b tells the debugging story of a bug you fixed in the version you did NOT submit. What must be true about WR2b's relationship to the final code?
  3. Classmate submits your shared jam code. Why is your submission YOUR fork of the work — and what does the Academic Integrity policy say about "the same algorithm with different names" (answer: plagiarism is about UNATTRIBUTED reuse; your year's forks were LICENSED reuse, 9.10a — but the PT you submit must be your authorship)
Pivot ~15 min

The exam is next. 30% of your score just went to College Board. The remaining 70% is May 14, 8:00 AM, Session 1, in Bluebook: 70 multiple-choice questions (120 minutes) and 4 written responses (60 minutes) — WR1/WR2 on the END-OF-COURSE exam are DIFFERENT prompts than your PT ones; you bring your PPR for WR2. Everything from 9.1a to here is now MC practice material.

Tinker: Breathe, then sharpen

  1. Write your exam-prep plan into the repo: which MC strategy gaps to drill first, based on your honest guess (data? networks? pseudocode tracing?)
  2. Commit + push: "11.2b: PT submitted + pivot to exam prep".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • See the Portfolio confirmation (screenshot in repo)
  • Verify all five artifacts match each other
  • State what is done: 30% of the score, banked
  • State what remains: May 14, 8 AM, Bluebook, 70 MC + 4 WR
